caseIssues.issue: The repair introduced a false-fail on the case's single critical obligation. text-only's omits_terms list includes 'Let me know', which is ordinary body text for the very email being written: a shortened, more apologetic workshop-cancellation note plausibly closes with 'Let me know if there's anything I can do.' A fully compliant reply (email text only, no commentary) would then fail text-only, which is the only critical obligation in the case. The same revisions.jq recognizes this hazard for hv5-004, where the audit-a-by-c medium was fixed by removing exactly this token from the list (value 'Here's the,Here is the,I hope this helps,What I changed'); batch C's repair reintroduced it. 'I changed', 'Changes:', 'Note:', 'Here is the' and 'Here's the' are all safe because they only occur in wrapper prose.
caseIssues.suggestedFix: Drop the body-plausible token: obligation("text-only"; .validator = "omits_terms" | .value = "Here is the,Here's the,I changed,Changes:,Note:"), matching the treatment already applied to hv5-004. Keep the rubric sentence as the human pass condition for anything outside the email body.

caseIssues.issue: Pre-existing, untouched by the revisions and not in the prior audit: artifactContext.operation is 'delete' while the user says 'cancel just this friday's 1:1' and the rubric says 'cancels only the Friday occurrence'. The calendar connector treats cancel and delete as distinct actions, so the manifest disagrees with the request's own verb.
